opening_fact.text: I was attacked by two men.

patient_facts.text: The attack happened about 3 hours ago.

patient_facts.text: It happened outside her regular bar.

patient_facts.text: The two men are strangers to her: she has seen them in the bar but never talked to them.

additional_considerations.rationale: Air or blood in the pleural space, possible after physical trauma; look for unilateral loss of breath sounds with hyperresonance, tracheal shift and JVD, and evaluate quickly with a chest X-ray.
Chest pain in trauma victims may be musculoskeletal in origin.

source_issues: Age conflict: the opening scenario says 27 years old; the SP-sheet patient description and the note HPI say 25. Demographics use 27 from the opening scenario.
Doorway temperature '98.0°F (36.0°C)': 98.0°F is 36.7°C; the Celsius value is wrong.

Three gold history findings exist only in the note, not in the script: no condom use (gold #2), possible ejaculation and LMP 3 weeks ago (gold #3). They were added as flagged note-only facts (f012, f013, f015).

The note HPI omits the abdominal pain ('it hurts everywhere', p027) and the wrist pain (p028); the note exam records a nontender abdomen and no wrist or skin findings, although the checklist includes a musculoskeletal inspection and palpation.
e005 ('Breath sounds clear to auscultation bilaterally...') has no system label; it continues the Chest line and is labeled Chest.
e004 'Tympanic to percussion throughout lung fields' is unusual (normal lung is resonant; hyperresonance would suggest pneumothorax) and no side is given; kept as written with a flag (x007).
e007 'G > BS x 4 quadrants' is a garbled symbol (probably '+ BS'); recorded as present with a flag (x014).
e003 (HEENT) contains 'No JVD', a neck finding.
p006 asks about weapons; the answer (fists and bodies) does not explicitly deny a weapon.
p024: the denial of blood in stool or urine is uninformative because she has not used the bathroom since the assault.
Note HPI says the event happened 'as she was leaving a bar'; the script says outside her regular bar while walking toward her car, then pulled into a storage room.
annotator_notes: The assault narrative is coded symptoms/hpi with temporality historical (a past event); the resulting pain, dyspnea, palpitations and fatigue are current.
'I only feel fatigued' (p022) is split into absent numbness, absent weakness and present fatigue.
Note-only facts (no condom use, unsure about ejaculation, LMP 3 weeks ago) are things the patient would know and support the gold; they carry from_note and flags.

SP instructions that create observable findings (depressed/tearful appearance; right chest pain with deep inspiration, cough and palpation) are added as sp_notes exam records (x020-x023); weeping when asked about the assault is left as an acting note.
